newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-up $1-private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen steady to $1.00 per cwt higher amid continued strength linked to light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
"There's just no numbers, they can't find enough hogs," one Indiana dealer said of packers need to compete for hogs.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to the plant were seen at $59.50 and Illinois top prices at the plant could range $58.50 to $59.00, sources said.
Indiana/Ohio hog prices at the plant could range $58.00 to $58.50, the dealers said.

Lighter slaughter so far this week lent support to pork prices, but the lack of strong retail buying outside of light fill-in demand was not keeping pace with the cost of hogs, some sources noted. As a result, packer operating margins remained unprofitable, which meant slaughter could be cut further.
One packer buyer said weekly slaughter could be reduced by 10,000-20,000 head and operating hours at some plants reduced to four hours from six.

Hog slaughter Tuesday was estimated at 332,000 head, compared with 338,000 a week ago and 322,000 a year ago, USDA reported. The week-to-date slaughter at 617,000 head was down 4.0 percent from the same period a week ago at 643,000 and down 1.9 percent from a year ago at 629,000.
